title: Scripture and Obedience
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Scripture and obedience teaches that the proper response to God’s Word is faith-filled obedience. Scripture is not given merely to be heard, studied, admired, or discussed, but to be believed and lived before God.
summary: Scripture and obedience teaches that the proper response to God’s Word is faith-filled obedience. Scripture is not given merely to be heard, studied, admired, or discussed, but to be believed and lived before God.
christFocus: Jesus said that love for Him is shown in keeping His commandments. The obedient life does not earn salvation, but it displays living faith in the Savior who speaks, saves, and leads His people.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God’s Word calls for response. Hearing without doing is self-deception. Scripture exposes truth not so people can admire it from a distance, but so they may trust God and walk in His ways.

Obedience flows from love and faith, not from self-saving pride. Believers obey because Christ is Lord, because His commands are good, and because grace trains His people to live differently.

Jesus compared the wise hearer to one who builds on the rock by hearing and doing His words. The foolish hearer hears but does not obey, and the collapse is great. Hearing without obedience is dangerous.

Scripture and obedience must be held together with the Gospel. Obedience does not earn acceptance with God, but those who have been saved by grace are called to submit their lives to the Word of the Lord.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Bible knowledge without obedience can produce pride, hypocrisy, or spiritual numbness. A person may quote Scripture, study doctrine, or attend teaching often while refusing to surrender to what God says.

This doctrine calls believers away from empty familiarity with the Bible. God’s Word is meant to reshape choices, speech, desires, relationships, worship, repentance, and trust in Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask not only, “What does this passage mean?” but also, “How must I respond?” Obey what God clearly shows you. When Scripture confronts sin, repent. When it commands love, act. When it calls for trust, believe. Do not obey to earn grace; obey because Christ is Lord and His grace has made you His own.
